source.citation: Pérez-Salado Kamps and Maurer (1996), J. Chem. Eng. Data 41, 1505-1513

source_findings.constant: K = a_MDEA a_H+ / a_MDEAH+, molality scale, solutes at infinite dilution in water (Eq. 8)
source_findings.fit_quality: average deviation 0.9 % (0.004 in pK), maximum 2 % (0.009) in K; water impurity of 1.6 mass % would lower K by about 2 %
source_findings.pressure: influence of pressure on the reactions neglected (p. 1509); no separate standard pressure is defined

criterion: reproduce ln K_x of Uyan 2015 Table 1 (and the Jakobsen 2005 table, see reaction-basis-interim.json) at printed precision, and give pK_m = 8.55 at 298.15 K
result: Uyan's mole-fraction law is Eq. 12 shifted by -4.0165 = ln(M_w m°): -79.474 - 4.0165 = -83.4905 against Uyan's -83.491; ln T coefficient 10.9756 against 10.976. The remaining difference is the rounding of 10.976.
conventions_for_stage_2: H+ is written as H3O+ with water activity, as for the MEA R5 law (Bates and Pinching, also an H+ form)
use the MEA R4/R5 source standard pressure convention of 100 kPa; the source neglects pressure
the law is measured to 368 K; states at 373-393 K use it as an extrapolation, as the MEA paper does for R4 and R5 above 323 K
